meta_title: Area Bounded by y²=x, x=1 to x=4 (NCERT Ex 8.1 Q1)
meta_desc: NCERT Class 12 Ex 8.1 Q1 solved: the area bounded by y²=x, x=1, x=4 and the x-axis is 14/3. Try the free 8-question area-by-integration quiz below.

quiz.title: Area by Integration Quiz (NCERT Ex 8.1 Q1)
quiz.intro: Eight questions on finding area under y=√x between x=1 and x=4. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: Area under a curve using definite integration

questions.q: The upper half of the parabola y²=x (the part above the x-axis) is described by which function?
questions.explanation: Solving y²=x for the branch where y is non-negative gives y = +√x, so the region above the x-axis sits under y = √x.

questions.q: For a curve y=f(x) with f≥0, the area enclosed by the curve, the x-axis and the lines x=a and x=b is given by:
options: ∫ from a to b of y dx
∫ from a to b of x dy
π ∫ from a to b of y² dx
∫ from a to b of y² dx
questions.explanation: Area between the curve and the x-axis over [a, b] is the definite integral of y with respect to x, i.e. ∫ from a to b of y dx.
Write √x as x^(1/2). Raise the power by 1 to x^(3/2) and divide by 3/2, giving (2/3)x^(3/2) + C.
The antiderivative is (2/3)x^(3/2). At x=4 it is 16/3, at x=1 it is 2/3, and 16/3 − 2/3 = 14/3.

questions.q: What is the value of (2/3)x^(3/2) at x=4?
What is the value of (2/3)x^(3/2) at x=1?
The area of the region bounded by y²=x, x=1, x=4 and the x-axis is:
questions.explanation: Area = ∫ from 1 to 4 of √x dx = [(2/3)x^(3/2)] from 1 to 4 = 16/3 − 2/3 = 14/3 square units.

questions.q: A region lies under y=√x from x=1 to x=4. Which definite integral gives its area?
questions.explanation: The height at each x is y=√x and the limits are x=1 and x=4, so the area is ∫ from 1 to 4 of √x dx.

faq.q: Why does y²=x become y=√x in this problem?
faq.a: The region asked for lies above the x-axis, where y is positive. Taking the positive square root of y²=x gives y=√x, which is the boundary of that region.

faq.q: What is the final area for NCERT Ex 8.1 Q1?
faq.a: The area bounded by y²=x, the lines x=1 and x=4, and the x-axis is 14/3 square units, found by evaluating the integral of √x from x=1 to x=4.
Rewrite √x as x^(1/2), then use the power rule: add 1 to the exponent to get x^(3/2) and divide by 3/2. The result is (2/3)x^(3/2) + C.

faq.q: Do I need to sketch the region before integrating?
faq.a: A quick sketch helps you confirm the curve stays above the x-axis over [1, 4], so the integral is positive and no splitting into parts is needed. It is good exam practice even when not asked.
